title: loadSave/applyGameSave have no save-version guard: a save written by a newer engine is loaded directly (downgrade corruption), and old saves are never migrated
detail: SaveMetadata.version is written from ENGINE_VERSION (4.0.5) on save (lines 94/102/220) but loadSave (line 137-162) never reads meta.version, and its only caller save-manager/page.tsx (line 38-41) calls applyGameSave(data) with zero version comparison or migration. autoMigrateFromDir exists but is only run for mod localStorage in init-mods-bootstrap, never for these OPFS saves. Concrete failure: a user on engine 5.x creates a save, then opens it on an older 4.0.5 build (or after a downgrade) — the newer-shaped state is fed straight into setState, producing a corrupt in-memory game with missing/renamed fields and no warning. Conversely an old 1.x save is loaded with no migration applied.
triggerPath: Confirmed against the real code. loadSave (save-manager.ts:137-162) loads meta and attaches it as data._meta (line 143) but never compares meta.version to ENGINE_VERSION; it returns the raw snapshot. applyGameSave (save-restore.ts:26-75) ignores data._meta entirely and feeds each store section directly into setState — e.g. useEngineStore.setState spreads `...engine` over prev (lines 29-39), and useCharacterStore/useWorldStore/useEconomyStore/etc. do full-object setState replacement (lines 44-65) with no version reconciliation. Both callers (save-manager/page.tsx:38-41 and welcome/page.tsx:69-71) call loadSave then applyGameSave(data) with zero version gating. autoMigrateFromDir (migration-runner.ts:162) only operates on localStorage keyed by mod name (lines 167-168,199) and is invoked solely in init-mods-bootstrap.ts:134 for mod stores — it cannot and does not touch OPFS save snapshots. The save-manager.ts header comment (lines 16-18) explicitly promises version-mismatch migration via 'save-version.ts', but that file does not exist (glob found nothing), so the migration is documented-but-unimplemented. Concrete reachable path: a save written under a newer ENGINE_VERSION opened on an older 4.0.5 build (or after downgrade) is fed straight into setState, producing corrupt in-memory state (missing/renamed fields) with no warning; conversely an old-shaped save loaded into a newer build gets no migration. The only mitigation present is a handful of hardcoded engine-field fallbacks (save-restore.ts:34-38), which protect a few known engine fields but not the other stores. Severity corrected to medium: within any single shipped version all saves share ENGINE_VERSION so no corruption occurs, and true downgrade corruption requires the uncommon newer-then-older run sequence; the realistic everyday risk is the silently-skipped upgrade migration.
fix: In loadSave (or at the top of applyGameSave) read meta.version (already available as data._meta.version): if compareVersions(meta.version, ENGINE_VERSION) > 0, throw a clear error refusing to load a newer save (preventing downgrade corruption); if older, run the migration chain (implement the promised save-version migration, analogous to autoMigrateFromDir but operating on the OPFS snapshot object) before passing data to the stores. compareVersions already exists in store-migration.

title: StorageNamespace.getAll reads global localStorage directly instead of the injected baseStorage, breaking isolation when baseStorage is not window.localStorage
detail: get/set/delete all go through the injected `baseStorage` (lines 34/44/48), but getAll (lines 51-68) ignores baseStorage and iterates the real global `localStorage` (`localStorage.length`, `localStorage.key(i)`, `localStorage.getItem`). If baseStorage is any other IStorageService implementation (in-memory test double, a prefixed/sandboxed wrapper, sessionStorage, or a mod-scoped store), getAll returns entries from the wrong backing store — missing data written via baseStorage.set and/or leaking other mods' raw keys. Concrete failure: a unit test or alternate runtime injects a fake storage; set('x',1) writes to the fake, getAll() returns {} or unrelated window keys, so any code relying on getAll to enumerate its own namespace silently sees nothing.
triggerPath: Confirmed real. storage-namespace.ts:34/44/48 route get/set/delete through the injected `baseStorage`, but getAll (lines 53-57) iterates the global `localStorage` (localStorage.length / .key(i) / .getItem) and filters by the bare `${modName}:` prefix. This is not academic: in production `context.storage` is NOT window.localStorage. In src/app/_components/init-mods-bootstrap.ts:49-53 it is a wrapper over `configStore` (src/core/storage/local-storage.ts), which rewrites every key. Concrete path: a mod calls myStorage.set('x', 1) -> baseStorage.setItem('mod-foo:x','1') -> configStore.set('app','mod-foo:x',1) -> write('app:config:mod-foo:x') -> real localStorage key = 'ai-life-sim:app:config:mod-foo:x'. Then myStorage.getAll() scans global localStorage for keys starting with 'mod-foo:' — but the actual stored key starts with 'ai-life-sim:app:config:mod-foo:x', so it never matches. getAll() therefore returns {} despite data having been written, and could also surface raw unrelated keys if any happened to share the prefix. The root cause is structural: IStorageService (src/foundation/types/mod.types.ts:229-233) exposes only getItem/setItem/removeItem with no key-enumeration method, so getAll cannot iterate baseStorage and silently falls back to the global object. Caveat on severity: no MOD in the repo currently calls the namespace getAll() (the many getAll* grep hits are unrelated subsystem methods like getAllSettlements / pattern-registry.getAll), and there are no tests injecting a fake store, so nothing is broken at runtime today — it is a latent correctness bug / isolation hole waiting for the first caller. Medium is fair; one could argue low given zero live callers. The reviewer's claim and suggested fix are accurate.
fix: Add a key-enumeration method to IStorageService (e.g. keys(): string[], or getAll()/entries()), implement it in the configStore-backed wrapper in init-mods-bootstrap.ts (enumerating its own backing keys with the correct 'ai-life-sim:app:config:' transform), and rewrite StorageNamespace.getAll to iterate baseStorage.keys() filtered by `${prefix}` instead of touching the global localStorage. This makes getAll honor whatever IStorageService implementation is injected.

title: applyWorldDirection writes economy fields (priceIndex/volatility) that economy.applyChanges ignores and that are overwritten next advance
detail: applyToSub('economy', ['priceIndex', 'volatility'], mult) builds `changes = { priceIndex: round(val*mult) }` and commits it via the 'world-direction' source. But EconomySystem has no `volatility` field at all (typeof check skips it) and no applyChanges handler for `priceIndex` — applyChanges only handles wealthDelta/setTaxRate/assets/debts/tradeRoutes/currency/difficulty. So the world-direction market correction never reaches economy state. Even if it did, economy recomputes priceIndex from scratch every advance (`this.state.priceIndex = round(clamp(100 + currency.inflation*2, 20, 300))`, line 402), discarding any external write. Concrete trigger: AI narrative includes '繁荣'; _applyWorldDirectionFromNarrative sets direction.market and calls applyWorldDirection, which produces a priceIndex change that is silently dropped — the '繁荣/衰退/危机' market direction feature is dead for economy.
triggerPath: Verified the full code path. (1) EconomyState.createInitialState (economy-system.ts:84-108) has no `volatility` field and grep finds none anywhere in mod-economy, so in applyToSub (orchestrator-system.ts:175-194) the `typeof val === 'number'` check skips `volatility`, leaving only `{ priceIndex }` in `changes`. (2) The commit flows via applyRoundChanges([change],'world-direction') → RoundCommitBus.commit. `world-direction` is NOT in SCHEMA_VALIDATED_SOURCES and is not 'cross-domain' (round-commit-bus.ts:41-90), so the change is NOT rejected upstream — it passes through to economy.applyChanges. (3) EconomySystem.applyChanges (economy-system.ts:137-262) has no handler reading the `priceIndex` field; it handles yearsAdvanced/wealthDelta/setTaxRate/asset/debt/tradeRoute/currency/difficulty, plus a description-text fallback (extractDynamicAttrsFromNarrative) that only parses playerWealth/totalCirculation/inflation/taxRate/gini — never priceIndex. So the priceIndex change is silently dropped. (4) Even if applied, _advanceEconomyOneYear line 402 recomputes `priceIndex = round(clamp(100 + currency.inflation*2, 20, 300))` each advance, overwriting any external write. (5) Reachable trigger: AI narrative containing 繁荣/衰退/危机/恢复 → _applyWorldDirectionFromNarrative (lines 1795-1810) sets direction.market → applyWorldDirection (lines 196-198) → applyToSub('economy',['priceIndex','volatility'],mult). Callers at campaigns/default/index.ts:316 and orchestrator-system.ts:896 run this during normal rounds. The 繁荣/衰退/危机 market-direction feature is therefore dead for the economy subsystem. No crash or corruption, so medium severity is correct.
fix: Map the market multiplier to a field economy actually applies. Simplest: in applyWorldDirection's market branch, emit a currency inflation delta (e.g. changes = { inflation: (mult-1)*K }) and add a handler in EconomySystem.applyChanges that does `this.state.currency.inflation = clamp(this.state.currency.inflation + c.inflation, -20, 50)` (matching the existing extracted.inflation path). Since priceIndex is derived from inflation at line 402, this makes the world-direction market correction persist and visibly affect priceIndex. Alternatively add a direct priceIndex-bias field that line 402 incorporates instead of recomputing purely from inflation.

title: Cooldown-less macro cross-domain rules fire once per event in the batch, double-applying effects when multiple notable events share a keyword
detail: In _executeCrossDomainLinkage (orchestrator-system.ts lines 960-988) the kernel is dispatched once for the main SYSTEM_EVENT_BATCH event and then once per lastNotableEvents entry, accumulating all instructions. The data-condition rules (6-11) are deduped by cooldownRounds, but the 5 macro keyword rules (rules 1-5 in cross-domain-rules.ts) have NO cooldownRounds, so evaluateCrossDomainDispatch re-fires them for every event whose description matches. Concrete trigger: AI returns two notableEvents both containing '战争' (or '战争' appears in both the batch description and a notable event). Rule 2 (war-faction-mobility) then emits its `tensionDelta` and `migrationInflow` instructions twice in the same round, so conflict-cycle tension and population migration inflow are applied 2x (or 3x). Effects compound incorrectly with the number of similarly-worded AI events.
triggerPath: The claim is confirmed end-to-end. (1) Rules 1-5 in cross-domain-rules.ts have NO cooldownRounds field; in simulation-kernel.ts the cooldown guard (lines 56-59) and the cooldown-set (lines 64-66) only execute when rule.cooldownRounds > 0, so the macro keyword rules are never deduped across dispatches in the same round. (2) In _executeCrossDomainLinkage (orchestrator-system.ts 960-988) the kernel is invoked once for the SYSTEM_EVENT_BATCH event and once per lastNotableEvents entry, all with the SAME round number, and every result is accumulated into one instructions array (instructions.push(...) at 967 and 987). (3) Rule 2 (war-faction-mobility) has eventTypePattern '*' and no dataCondition; its condition matches any description containing '战争'/'冲突'/etc. Two AI notable events sharing such a keyword (e.g. lastNotableEvents = ['北方爆发战争','边境战争升级'], set at line 873 from AI output) each fire rule 2, producing two tensionDelta:10 and two migrationInflow:5 instructions. A single notable event whose keyword also appears in the batch description triggers the same double-fire. (4) Neither the validator nor the commit path dedups: validateCrossDomainChanges (cross-domain-change-validator.ts 157-164) processes each change independently, and RoundCommitBus.commit (round-commit-bus.ts 52-128) loops over commit.changes and calls applyChange for EACH change with no per-(system,field) merge. (5) The downstream subsystems apply these deltas additively/compoundingly: conflict-cycle-system.ts line 189 does state.tension = clamp(tension + tensionDelta) (so +20 instead of +10), and population-system.ts line 142-149 unshifts a separate migration record per invocation (two refugee records instead of one). Thus the effects genuinely double-apply. The defect is real and reachable; severity medium is appropriate (no crash, values are clamped, but simulation deltas are silently inflated proportional to the number of similarly-worded AI events).
fix: Deduplicate macro-rule firing per round. Minimal option: give rules 1-5 in cross-domain-rules.ts a cooldownRounds of 1, so the kernel records cooldowns[rule.id]=round on first fire and skips subsequent dispatches in the same round (the orchestrator already threads cooldowns across the batch+notable-event dispatches via the cooldowns variable at lines 956/966/986). Alternatively, dedupe the accumulated instructions array in _executeCrossDomainLinkage before applyRoundChanges by collapsing entries with the same (rule/sourceEventId-independent) targetSystemId+param-key, but the cooldownRounds:1 approach is smaller and consistent with how rules 6-11 are already guarded.

title: Active events ranked outside the top-3 by severity are dropped from the lifecycle tracker, resetting their continuity counter
detail: buildEventInjectionText only writes the top 3 raw events (topActive = rawEvents.slice(0,3)) into newLifecycle (loop at line 363). The second loop over prev (line 395) does `if (activeTypes.has(eventType)) continue` — and activeTypes is built from ALL rawEvents, not just the top 3. So a previously-tracked event that is still active this round but ranks #4+ by severity is skipped in BOTH loops and therefore disappears from newLifecycle entirely. Next round, if it re-enters the top 3, prev[e.eventType] is undefined so it is reported as '新发生' (new) with consecutiveRounds reset to 1, even though it never actually ended. Concrete trigger: 4+ simultaneous active events (e.g. 市场崩溃 0.7, 生态崩溃 0.8, 边境冲突 0.7, plus 通货膨胀 0.5) — the 0.5 event is dropped and loses its ongoing/duration tracking. Recovery thresholds for that type are also never evaluated.
triggerPath:
The defect is real and reachable. Concrete trigger: a round with 4+ simultaneous active events where one previously-tracked event is displaced to rank #4+ by severity.

Code path in buildEventInjectionText (event-lifecycle-tracker.ts):
1. Line 357: activeTypes is built from ALL rawEvents.
2. Line 360-361: rawEvents sorted desc by severity, topActive = slice(0,3).
3. Loop 1 (line 363) iterates only topActive — the #4+ event is skipped, so it is NOT written to newLifecycle here.
4. Loop 2 (line 395) iterates all prev. For the #4+ event, record.status is 'ongoing'/'new' (not 'ending'), so it reaches line 404: `if (activeTypes.has(eventType)) continue`. Since the event IS active (in rawEvents), this continues, skipping it. So it is also NOT written to newLifecycle here.

Result: the still-active #4+ event disappears from newLifecycle entirely. Its recovery threshold is never evaluated, and its lifecycle record (firstSeenRound, consecutiveRounds, peakSeverity) is lost.

Persistence across rounds is confirmed: orchestrator-system.ts line 791-796 stores newLifecycle into this.eventLifecycle and feeds it back as lastLifecycle next round (also at campaigns/default/index.ts:90-95). So next round prev[eventType] is undefined; if the event re-enters top 3 it falls into the else branch at line 378-390 and is reported as '新发生' with consecutiveRounds reset to 1, despite never having ended.

Reachability: detectRawEvents pushes up to 14 independent event types (10 macro + 4 character-driven) with no cap; the only limiter is slice(0,3). The DETAIL's example (市场崩溃 0.7, 生态崩溃 0.8, 边境冲突 0.7, 通货膨胀 0.5) is achievable, dropping the 0.5 event. The bug is genuine. Severity medium is appropriate: it only corrupts continuity/recovery tracking for the 4th+ event (no crash, and the top-3 displayed events are unaffected).
fix: In loop 2 (line 404), instead of unconditionally `continue` when the event is still active but not in topActive, carry it forward as ongoing. Replace `if (activeTypes.has(eventType)) continue` with: if activeTypes.has(eventType) and eventType is not already in newLifecycle (i.e. it was displaced out of topActive), write a carried-forward ongoing record — e.g. `if (activeTypes.has(eventType)) { if (!newLifecycle[eventType]) newLifecycle[eventType] = { ...record, status: 'ongoing', lastSeenRound: round, consecutiveRounds: record.consecutiveRounds + 1 }; continue }`. This keeps the tracker state complete for all active events while leaving injectedLines (the displayed text) limited to top-3.

title: characterCreations array only ever grows and is injected in full into every prompt's stable segment (unbounded memory + prompt bloat)
detail: handleNarrativeResponse pushes every new AI-declared creation into this.state.characterCreations with name-based dedup but no length cap (lines 1609-1621). buildCreationProtectionText (lines 1299-1311) and buildUserInstruction (lines 1460-1463) then list ALL accumulated creations into the prompt every single round. Over a long simulation with a creative character the array grows without bound, is structuredCloned on every captureSnapshot/getState, serialized into every auto-save payload, and inflates the prompt token count every round (defeating the KV-cache 'stable' segment intent once it changes). Unlike narrativeHistory (capped at MAX_NARRATIVE_HISTORY, lines 1654-1656) there is no trimming.
triggerPath: Confirmed reachable in orchestrator-system.ts. handleNarrativeResponse (lines 1609-1621) pushes every AI-parsed creation (effectiveParsed.creations, originating from AI JSON output per narrative-parser-system.ts:85) into this.state.characterCreations with name-based dedup ONLY — no length cap, no trim, no summarization. The very next block (lines 1653-1656) trims narrativeHistory with `while (length > MAX_NARRATIVE_HISTORY) shift()` (=200), proving the pattern exists but was not applied to characterCreations. The full array is re-injected into the prompt every round via two paths: buildCreationProtectionText (lines 1299-1311, wired at line 1175 into the stable creationProtectionText segment) maps the ENTIRE creations array to prompt lines, and buildUserInstruction (lines 1460-1462) joins ALL creation names into another prompt line. The array is also copied into save/snapshot payloads (line 2103 and hooks.ts:36). Concrete trigger: a long simulation where the AI introduces many distinct-named creations over time — each unique name is a permanent entry, growing memory, save size, and per-round prompt token count without bound. No upstream guard, not dead code, the parse-and-push path is exercised on every round that returns a non-empty creations field. The 'defeats KV-cache stable segment' framing is consistent (stable-segment content changes as creations accumulate), not a refutation. Severity medium is correct: gradual cost/memory degradation over long sessions, not a crash.
fix: Mirror the narrativeHistory trim: after the push loop (after line 1621), add a cap such as `while (this.state.characterCreations.length > MAX_CHARACTER_CREATIONS) this.state.characterCreations.shift()` with a new constant (e.g. 50). Additionally/alternatively, in buildCreationProtectionText (line 1302) and buildUserInstruction (line 1461) only emit the most-recent N entries (e.g. creations.slice(-N)) so the per-round prompt stays bounded even if the full set is retained for save integrity.

title: When all 5 slots are occupied the dialog recommends slot 1 and pre-selects it, leading to silent overwrite of the slot-1 save
detail: nextSlotRaw = getNextSlot() returns max(slot)+1; with slots 1-5 all used (and auto-save at slot 0) it returns 6. `const nextSlot = nextSlotRaw > 5 ? 1 : nextSlotRaw` collapses that to 1, and activeSlot defaults to it. The UI then labels slot 1 as the recommended slot ('推荐使用槽位 1') and the default save target. A user who accepts the recommendation overwrites their existing slot-1 save. There is a warning chip, but the recommendation actively steers the user toward destroying the oldest manual save rather than, say, the least-recently-used or a confirmed choice.
triggerPath: Confirmed the mechanics in SaveDialog.tsx and save-manager.ts. getNextSlot() (save-manager.ts:245-249) returns max(slot)+1 over listSaves()/loadIndex(), which includes the auto-save slot 0 plus manual slots. With manual slots 1-5 all occupied, max is 5 so it returns 6. Line 32 `const nextSlot = nextSlotRaw > 5 ? 1 : nextSlotRaw` collapses 6 to 1. The `slot` state defaults to 1 (line 26), so activeSlot=1 (line 33). The caller (game-story/page.tsx:528-534) passes no prop that resets this, and there is no useEffect resetting slot on open — so on every open with all slots full, slot 1 is the active/highlighted default and line 107 prints '推荐使用槽位 1'. handleManualSave (page.tsx:462-465) calls saveManager.saveToSlot directly with no separate confirm dialog. So a user who fills slots 1-5 and accepts the recommendation does overwrite the existing slot-1 save. Concrete trigger: occupy manual slots 1-5, open SaveDialog -> nextSlot=1, slot 1 pre-selected and labeled '推荐使用槽位 1', clicking Save overwrites slot 1. The defect (recommending and pre-selecting an occupied slot rather than requiring an explicit pick or recommending LRU) is real and reachable. However the 'silent overwrite' framing is overstated: occupied===true so the warning chip renders ('槽位 1 已有存档，保存会覆盖原内容' lines 90/127-130) and the action button label changes to '覆盖保存' (line 152). The overwrite is therefore signalled, not silent, which is why I downgrade severity to low — it is a misleading-default UX bug, not silent data loss.
fix: When all five manual slots are full, do not default the active slot to an occupied one. Minimal fix in SaveDialog.tsx: detect the all-full case and, instead of collapsing to slot 1, either (a) recommend the least-recently-saved manual slot (e.g. derive from saveManager.listSaves() sorted by timestamp ascending, picking the oldest manual slot 1-5) and surface it as the recommendation, and (b) leave activeSlot unselected (require an explicit click) so the user makes a deliberate overwrite choice. Concretely replace `const nextSlot = nextSlotRaw > 5 ? 1 : nextSlotRaw` with logic that, when nextSlotRaw > 5, computes the oldest occupied manual slot via timestamp and treats the all-full state as 'no recommended free slot' (e.g. label it '所有槽位已满，请选择要覆盖的槽位' rather than '推荐使用槽位 1'), and initialize slot state to null/unselected requiring an explicit pick before enabling the save button.

title: narrativeEntries memo omits stratumLabel/streaming-related values but mainly carries a stale resolvedBranches→index coupling risk after history truncation
detail: `narrativeEntries` maps `narrativeHistory` and reads `resolvedChoice: chunk.resolvedChoice ?? resolvedBranches[index]`, where `index` is the absolute array index. The engine store persists only the last 50 chunks (store.ts partialize slices narrativeHistory to the last 50) while `resolvedBranches` is a `Record<number,string>` keyed by the original absolute index and is NOT re-keyed on truncation. After a reload where more than 50 narrative chunks existed, the in-memory `narrativeHistory` indices are shifted (old index N becomes N-k) but `resolvedBranches` still holds the old keys, so `resolvedBranches[index]` either resolves to the wrong branch choice or to undefined for the entry that actually was a resolved branch point. Trigger: play past 50 rounds with at least one resolved branch in the first chunks, reload; resolved-branch labels attach to the wrong timeline entry. (chunk.resolvedChoice mitigates this for chunks that had it written back via resolveBranch, but entries relying on the resolvedBranches fallback are affected.)
triggerPath:
Confirmed the data flow. In store.ts, partialize slices narrativeHistory to the last 50 (line 171-172) but never re-keys or truncates resolvedBranches (a Record<number,string> keyed by absolute index, persisted whole via ...rest). page.tsx:373 reads `resolvedChoice: chunk.resolvedChoice ?? resolvedBranches[index]` with index = post-truncation absolute array index.

The claim's PRIMARY framing is NOT triggerable: resolveBranch (store.ts:149-156) atomically writes BOTH resolvedBranches[index] AND chunk.resolvedChoice into the chunk. The chunk (with its resolvedChoice) survives truncation intact, and the `??` short-circuits to the chunk's own value. So a resolved branch that survives truncation ALWAYS shows the correct choice and NEVER falls back to the mis-keyed resolvedBranches[index]; it also can never resolve to undefined. The "labels attach to the wrong entry / undefined" scenarios are dead paths.

However, ONE narrow path is genuinely reachable and produces a wrong UI: the render gate (NarrativeTimeline.tsx:177) is `entry.isBranchPoint && entry.resolvedChoice`. A chunk that lacks its own resolvedChoice but is an UNRESOLVED branch point (isBranchPoint true) will display a phantom "你的选择: <stale>" if resolvedBranches[index] holds a leftover key. handleNarrativeAdvance (page.tsx:359) blocks advancing while hasUnresolvedBranch, so an unresolved branch is always the final chunk (index = length-1 = 49 after truncation to 50). Concrete trigger: resolve a branch when history length was 50 (writes resolvedBranches[49]); play 50+ more rounds until reaching a new branch that is currently unresolved (lands at new index 49); reload. On restore, the unresolved final branch at index 49 reads stale resolvedBranches[49] and renders a phantom "你的选择" with a choice the player never made for that branch. Non-branch chunks are unaffected (gated by isBranchPoint), so the impact is limited to this cosmetic phantom-label case — consistent with low severity.
fix: Drop the `resolvedBranches[index]` fallback and rely solely on `chunk.resolvedChoice`, i.e. `resolvedChoice: chunk.resolvedChoice` at page.tsx:373 (and remove resolvedBranches from the memo deps). resolveBranch already writes resolvedChoice into every resolved chunk, so the fallback is redundant for current saves and is the sole source of the stale-index collision. (Caveat: this could regress display only for legacy saves created before the chunk-writeback existed; if those must be supported, instead re-key resolvedBranches by a stable chunk id/timestamp on truncation.)

title: Virtual window is not applied on initial mount when entries are already populated (e.g. after save-load)
detail: `prevTotalRef` is initialized to `entries.length` and `renderStart` to 0. The window effect only shrinks the render range when `total > prevTotalRef.current`. On first mount after a save restore (where restoreSnapshot repopulates narrativeHistory in one shot), `entries.length` is already e.g. 50 and equals prevTotalRef, so the `total > prevTotalRef` branch never runs and the else-branch keeps renderStart at min(0, ...) = 0. Result: all 50+ entries (each splitting text into paragraphs + attrChanges chips) render at once instead of the intended 30-entry WINDOW_SIZE, defeating the virtualization right after a load. Trigger: load a save with >30 narrative entries; the whole history mounts un-windowed.
triggerPath:
Concrete reachable path confirmed. Save-load flow: welcome/page.tsx handleContinue (line 67-75) and save-manager/page.tsx handleLoad (line 36-46) both call applyGameSave(data) synchronously, which repopulates narrativeHistory in one shot (save-restore.ts via orchestrator.restoreSnapshot + engine hydration), THEN router.push('/game-story'). So NarrativeTimeline mounts only AFTER narrativeHistory is already fully populated. In game-story/page.tsx, narrativeEntries maps 1:1 from narrativeHistory (line 365-377) and NarrativeTimeline is rendered unconditionally (line 882) with no guard delaying it.

In NarrativeTimeline.tsx: prevTotalRef = useRef(entries.length) initializes to the full count (e.g. 50); renderStart state = 0. The mount effect (line 71-83) computes total=50; total===0 false; total > prevTotalRef.current is 50 > 50 = FALSE, so the else branch runs: setRenderStart(prev => Math.min(0, Math.max(0, 50-30))) = Math.min(0, 20) = 0. renderStart stays 0. The eventElements memo loops from i=renderStart=0 to entries.length, rendering all 50 entries (each splitting text into paragraphs + attrChange chips) instead of the intended last 30 (renderStart should be 20). Virtualization is defeated on the post-load mount.

React StrictMode does not mask it: on a second effect invocation prevTotalRef.current is still 50 and total still 50, so the growth branch still never fires. The defect is genuinely triggered whenever a save with >30 narrative entries is loaded. Severity 'low' is appropriate: it is a virtualization/performance degradation (extra DOM nodes), not a crash or data corruption.
fix: In the window effect, clamp renderStart on every run regardless of growth direction. Replace the if/else (lines 77-81) with a single: setRenderStart(prev => total > prevTotalRef.current ? Math.max(0, total - WINDOW_SIZE) : Math.min(prev, Math.max(0, total - WINDOW_SIZE))) — but since on initial mount prev is 0 and Math.min keeps it at 0, the real fix is to either initialize prevTotalRef to 0 (so the first run takes the growth branch and sets renderStart = total - WINDOW_SIZE), or unconditionally run setRenderStart(prev => Math.max(0, Math.min(prev > 0 ? prev : total, total - WINDOW_SIZE))). Simplest concrete fix: initialize const prevTotalRef = useRef(0); the first effect run then sees total (50) > 0 and sets renderStart = Math.max(0, 50-30) = 20, applying the window immediately.

title: Streaming passthrough logs status 200 before stream completes and forwards no upstream errors that occur mid-stream
detail: For streaming, `writeAccessLog(providerId, model, 200, ...)` is called at line 364 and then the raw `upstreamResp.body` is returned at lines 367-374. The 200 is logged at the moment headers arrive, before any body is read, so an upstream that returns 200 headers then errors/cuts off mid-stream is recorded as a successful 200 with a duration that only measures time-to-headers. More importantly the body is piped verbatim with `Cache-Control: no-cache` but the proxy cannot observe or surface a mid-stream upstream failure (it has already returned). Failure scenario: provider sends 200 + opening SSE frames then drops the connection; access log shows status 200 success and duration ~ms, masking the failure during debugging.
triggerPath:
The code at src/app/api/proxy/route.ts:364-375 matches the claim exactly and the described behavior is concretely reachable. For a streaming request (isStream && upstreamResp.body truthy), control reaches line 364 which calls writeAccessLog(providerId, model, 200, duration, ...) where `duration = Date.now() - startTime` is computed at line 328 immediately after `await fetch(...)` resolves — i.e. when response HEADERS arrive, before any body byte is read. Then lines 367-374 return `new Response(upstreamResp.body, ...)` verbatim, with no TransformStream, tee, or completion callback. Concrete trigger: a provider that returns HTTP 200 with opening SSE frames then drops/errors the connection mid-stream. The access log (logs/proxy-access-<date>.jsonl, written by writeAccessLogAsync) will contain {status:200, duration_ms:<time-to-headers>, error:''}, because the proxy has already returned the Response object and has no further visibility into the byte stream. The proxy cannot observe or surface the mid-stream failure. So the logging/observability defect is real and reachable as stated.

However, this is strictly a log-fidelity / observability limitation, not a functional correctness bug: returning upstreamResp.body directly is the correct passthrough behavior — the end client still receives exactly the bytes (and the same truncation) the upstream produced; there is no wrong response delivered, no crash, no data corruption. The only wrong artifact is the access-log entry recording a premature 200 and a too-short duration. Because the impact is confined to debugging/metrics accuracy and the user-facing data path is correct, medium overstates it; low is appropriate. The async fire-and-forget writeAccessLog (line 196 `void writeAccessLogAsync`) does not change this — it is intended and swallows its own errors.
fix: Wrap the upstream body in a TransformStream before returning, accumulating byte count and capturing stream end/abort. On `flush` (normal completion) or on a stream error/cancel, write a second access-log entry recording the final status (e.g. 200 'completed' with byte count and full duration, or 'aborted' if the readable errors). Minimal version: log streaming entries with a status like 'opened' at line 364, then attach `.pipeThrough(new TransformStream({ flush(){ writeAccessLog(..., 'completed', Date.now()-startTime, ...) } }))` (plus a try/catch or reader error handler to log 'aborted') so a mid-stream drop is recorded instead of masked as a clean 200.

title: 429 retry path discards retryAfter; backoff ignores provider Retry-After hint
detail: On HTTP 429 the client throws `new Error('__RETRY_429__')` (lines 671-673 non-stream, 834-836 stream), a bare sentinel string with no payload. `executeAiFetchWithRetry` catches it and retries with `getBackoffDelay(attempt)` (line 627), but `getBackoffDelay`'s `retryAfter` parameter (lines 583-586) is never supplied because the 429 error carries no retryAfter value — even though the proxy DID parse and return `retryAfter` in the JSON body (route.ts:347-358). So the client always backs off with the fixed RETRY_DELAY_MS*(attempt+1) ladder and ignores the server's explicit Retry-After, retrying sooner than the provider asked and risking repeated 429s / further rate-limit penalties.
triggerPath: Concrete reachable path: provider returns HTTP 429 with a JSON body containing a retryAfter field. (1) In route.ts:347-358 the proxy parses errData.retryAfter and forwards it in the 429 response body. (2) In ai-client.ts:671-673 (non-stream) and 834-836 (stream), the client checks resp.status===429 and immediately throws new Error('__RETRY_429__') WITHOUT ever reading resp.json()/resp.text(), so the retryAfter value in the body is discarded. (3) executeAiFetchWithRetry catches the error (line 622) and on retry calls getBackoffDelay(attempt) at lines 611 and 627 — always with a single argument. Grep confirms getBackoffDelay is never called with a second argument anywhere. (4) Therefore the retryAfter parameter and its branch `if (retryAfter) return retryAfter*1000` at lines 583-584 is dead code; the client always uses RETRY_DELAY_MS*(attempt+1). isRetryError only matches the sentinel string and carries no payload. No upstream guard or alternate header-reading path exists. The defect is genuinely triggerable. Impact is degraded behavior (backing off sooner than the provider's Retry-After hint, risking repeated 429s), not a crash; retries remain bounded by MAX_RETRY, so medium severity is on the high side but defensible — low/medium is the honest range.
fix: On 429, read the body before throwing and propagate retryAfter. E.g. in both fetchAIResponse and fetchAIStreamResponse: `if (resp.status === 429) { const body = await resp.json().catch(() => ({})); const e = new Error('__RETRY_429__'); (e as any).retryAfter = typeof body.retryAfter === 'number' ? body.retryAfter : undefined; throw e }`. Then in executeAiFetchWithRetry's catch, extract it: `const ra = (err as any)?.message === '__RETRY_429__' ? (err as any).retryAfter : undefined` and pass it: `getBackoffDelay(attempt, ra)`. The retryAfter param already exists at line 583, so only the propagation and the two call sites (611/627) need updating.

title: QuotaExceeded recovery only purges cache/temp and never frees space when the bloat is in save:/config:, so large save writes silently fail
detail: write() (lines 115-150) catches QuotaExceededError and removes only keys containing ':cache:' or ':temp:' (lines 133-137), explicitly preserving config: and save:. The save index itself is written through configStore.set -> write with a `save-manager:config:index` key. When the quota is actually consumed by save data (the common case once many slots exist), the cleanup frees little/nothing, the retry setItem (line 142) throws again, and the catch at 143-145 only console.errors — the function returns normally, so saveIndex() appears to succeed while the index was NOT persisted. The new save's OPFS files exist but the index update (e.g. a new slot pushed in saveToSlot line 108) is lost, so the save is invisible/orphaned with no surfaced error.
triggerPath:
I attempted to refute the claim by checking the storage architecture and failed: the defect is real and reachable, though the claim's stated *cause* is partly wrong.

Confirmed code facts:
- write() (src/core/storage/local-storage.ts:115-150) catches QuotaExceededError, and the cleanup loop (lines 128-140) only removes keys whose stripped form .includes(':cache:') or ':temp:'. save: and config: entries are deliberately preserved.
- After cleanup it retries setItem at line 142; if that throws again, the catch at 143-145 only console.errors and does NOT rethrow. write() always returns void.
- configStore.set -> write (lines 20-22) and thus saveManager.saveIndex (save-manager.ts:51-53) cannot observe failure.
- saveToSlot (save-manager.ts:80-120) calls saveIndex(metaList) at line 109 with no error handling, then writes the OPFS payload at lines 111-117. So a silently-failed index write yields OPFS files on disk with no corresponding index entry => orphaned/invisible save, no error surfaced to the user. autoSave (195-240) has the same shape.

Reachability of a full localStorage dominated by preserved keys: the claim says the bloat is "save data once many slots exist", which is INACCURATE — the large per-slot save snapshots (world.json/char.json/engine.json) go to OPFS (save-manager.ts:111-117), a separate backend with its own quota, never through this write(). However the defect is still reachable because saveStore IS used to persist sizable arrays directly in localStorage under save:0:* keys: world-timeline-system.ts stores timeline-stage / timeline-meta / past-history event arrays (lines 291,318,336), world-entity-system.ts stores the full entity list (line 571), world-map-system.ts stores world-map payloads (line 296), and these are keyed by worldCode so they accumulate across multiple worlds. All of these carry the save: prefix and are exactly what the cleanup routine refuses to evict. So a realistic path: user explores several worlds -> localStorage fills with save:0:timeline-*/entities/world-map entries -> a subsequent saveManager save triggers QuotaExceeded -> cleanup frees only cache/temp (little/nothing) -> retry of the index write throws -> swallowed -> saveToSlot still writes OPFS files -> save is orphaned and invisible in listSaves(), with only a console.error.

So: claim's mechanism (silent failure of the index write under quota pressure when the surviving bloat is save:/config:, producing an orphaned save with no surfaced error) is genuine; only its description of WHICH data fills localStorage is off (it's saveStore world-state arrays, not multi-slot save snapshots). The net behavioral defect stands and is triggerable.

Severity: low is appropriate — requires near-full localStorage (an edge state), and the impact is silent data inconsistency / lost save rather than a crash or active corruption of existing data.
fix: Make write() return a boolean (or throw) on final failure instead of swallowing it. Minimal: change write() to return false in the line 143-145 catch (and true on success/successful retry), have configStore.set/saveStore.set propagate that, and have saveManager.saveIndex() check the result — on failure, throw or return a failure so saveToSlot/autoSave can surface an error to the UI (and avoid leaving orphaned OPFS files, or roll them back). Optionally extend the quota cleanup to evict stale save:0:* world-cache entries (timeline/entities/world-map for non-active worlds) with the index itself being the last thing preserved.

title: Narrative age uses prevRoundYear-1 with year-unit time steps, lagging the character's reported age by a full step each round
detail: advanceTime() sets prevRoundYear = state.round.year BEFORE advancing (line 373), then computeNarrativeAge returns startingAge + max(0, prevRoundYear - 1) (line 390). For year-unit time steps where round.year jumps by N each turn (advanceYears), the age handed to the prompt and to useCharacterStore (syncCharacterStateForPrompt, line 726) reflects the year at the START of the turn, not the year being narrated. Concrete trigger: timeStep = {unit:'year', value:10}; after the round that advances year 11->21, the narrative still describes the character at age startingAge+10 while the world state (economy/population/lifespan) has already advanced 10 more simulated years, so the displayed age trails the simulated state by one full 10-year step. Lifespan/death narration can therefore reference an age inconsistent with the lifespan subsystem.
triggerPath:
The defect is real and reachable. Two age formulas diverge within the SAME prompt:

1. Orchestrator computeNarrativeAge (orchestrator-system.ts:384-390) uses prevRoundYear: `startingAge + max(0, prevRoundYear - 1)`. prevRoundYear is captured in advanceTime() (line 373) BEFORE round.year is advanced. This value feeds syncCharacterStateForPrompt (line 709 → character.age, useCharacterStore at line 726), coherenceHeader (line 1100), and lifeStageHint (line 1106-1111).

2. The lifespan subsystem getCharacterAge (mod-character/subsystems/lifespan-system.ts:297-303) uses the POST-advance year: `startingAge + max(0, context.round.year - 1)`, where buildRoundContext sets context.round = this.state.round (orchestrator line 689) — i.e. the already-advanced year. This age is baked into the lifespan subsystem `summary` ("当前年龄 X") at lines 59/84, which flows into rawStateSummaries → summaries → the prompt (orchestrator lines 1069-1078).

Concrete trigger (a supported config — time-system.ts:110 lists year × 1/3/5/10/...): timeStep={unit:'year',value:10}. advanceYears (time-system.ts:259-269) increments round.year by 10. For a round where round.year goes 11→21: prevRoundYear=11, round.year=21.
- Lifespan subsystem summary in the prompt reports age = startingAge + 21 - 1 = startingAge + 20.
- Character block / coherence header / life-stage hint report age = startingAge + 11 - 1 = startingAge + 10.
Same prompt, 10-year inconsistency. The lifespan/death narration (and life-stage hint, derived from maxAge vs. the trailing age) can therefore reference an age inconsistent with the lifespan subsystem's own stated age.

This is NOT guarded or intended: the comment at orchestrator-system.ts:704 explicitly states syncCharacterStateForPrompt is "与 lifespan 子系统公式一致" (consistent with the lifespan subsystem formula), but the formulas demonstrably are not consistent — one uses prevRoundYear, the other round.year. Even with year value=1 the lifespan summary is always 1 year ahead of the character block; multi-year steps widen the gap to the full step size. Effect is confined to prompt/narrative content (no crash or persisted-state corruption), so 'low' severity is appropriate.
fix: Pick one source of truth for narrative age and use it in both places. Cleanest: make computeNarrativeAge (orchestrator-system.ts:389) use the same post-advance year the lifespan subsystem uses — i.e. `const yearForAge = context.round.year` — so the character block matches the lifespan card. If the existing "首回合 advance 后仍描述 0 岁" baseline (age = startingAge after the first advance) must be preserved, instead change lifespan-system.ts:302 getCharacterAge to subtract the per-round simulation delta (or expose a shared helper, e.g. derive from prevRoundYear/ageYearsDelta) so both compute identical ages. Either way, both call sites must read the same year reference; the line-704 comment should then actually hold.

title: Economy summary reads population total before population advances this round (stale-by-one ordering)
detail: EconomySystem is registered before PopulationSystem (mod-economy/manifest.ts lists EconomySystem then PopulationSystem), so in collectSubsystemStates Round 1, economy.collectState runs first and reads context.subsystemStates['population'].totalPopulation — which is the value collected on the PREVIOUS orchestrator round (this round's population.collectState has not run yet). The economy-scale text / summary (getSummaryText -> getTotalEconomy uses totalPopulation) and the orchestrator's buildEconomyScaleText therefore report an economy-total computed against last round's population. Conversely population reads economy's already-updated marketPhase, so only one of the two cross-reads is current. Concrete trigger: a year-step round where population jumps significantly; the economy 'economy total / scale tier' shown to the AI lags one round behind the actual population.
triggerPath:
The defect is real and reachable for the economy subsystem's OWN summary string, though the claim overstates one detail.

Concrete code path:
1. manifest.ts (lines 17-23) registers EconomySystem before PopulationSystem; the orchestrator iterates `allSubs` in this order in collectSubsystemStates Round 1 (orchestrator-system.ts line 598-628).
2. In Round 1, EconomySystem.collectState (economy-system.ts line 110-134) reads `context.subsystemStates['population'].data.totalPopulation` (line 112-113). The `context` comes from buildRoundContext (orchestrator line 592), whose `subsystemStates` is `this.lastSubsystemStates` (line 692) — set only at line 676 AFTER the entire prior collectSubsystemStates run. So economy reads the PREVIOUS orchestrator round's population.
3. EconomySystem has NO collectStateUpdate / collectStateFinalFix (grep confirmed none), so it never re-reads population with the freshly-collected current-round value. Its `summary` (getSummaryText, line 504-524) embeds `经济总量：X（scale）` computed from getTotalEconomy(staleTotalPopulation) (line 456-458).
4. Conversely, PopulationSystem.advancePopulation (population-system.ts line 200-227) reads economy's marketPhase via _detectProsperity (line 306-313) from the same context — and since economy ran earlier in Round 1, population also reads last-round's economy state, but population then advances totalPopulation (line 227) this round. The cross-read asymmetry the reviewer describes holds.
5. This economy summary IS sent to the AI: assemblePromptContext builds `rawStateSummaries` from each state's `summary` (orchestrator line 1069-1072) and includes them in `summaries` (line 1075-1078) used in the prompt.

On a year-step round where population jumps (births/deaths scale with `years`, population-system line 223-224), the economy summary's `经济总量/scale tier` lags one round behind actual population. No crash, no upstream guard removes it, not dead code.

One correction to the claim: the orchestrator's buildEconomyScaleText (orchestrator line 1347-1368) reads BOTH economy.playerWealth and population.totalPopulation from `this.lastSubsystemStates` — i.e. the fully-completed current round — so ITS economy total is current and consistent, NOT stale. The reviewer wrongly named buildEconomyScaleText as also lagging. The genuinely stale value is the economy subsystem's own getSummaryText output. Net: the defect exists and is reachable, so isReal=true, but it is genuinely low severity (cosmetic one-round lag in one of two redundant economy-total texts shown to the AI).
fix: Make EconomySystem read the freshly-collected population by adding a collectStateUpdate(round1Context) that recomputes summary using context.subsystemStates['population'].data.totalPopulation (now current after Round 1), returning `{ id, summary }`; the orchestrator merges it (line 645). Alternatively, order PopulationSystem before EconomySystem in manifest.ts AND have the orchestrator's Round 1 read from the in-progress `states` map rather than lastSubsystemStates — but that is a larger change. The minimal fix is the collectStateUpdate override on EconomySystem that regenerates getSummaryText with the now-current totalPopulation.
